newsitem.title: USA: GM, UAW reach deal to end truck plant strike.
newsitem.headline: GM, UAW reach deal to end truck plant strike.

text.p: General Motors Corp and the United Auto Workers union reached a tentative agreement Wednesday night to end a nearly three-month strike at GM's truck plant here, one of the longest ever for the automaker.
UAW Local 594 President Ron Miller said the deal, reached just after 9:30 p.m. EDT Wednesday, provides additional jobs for the plant, which produces full-size Chevrolet and GMC pickup trucks.

About 5,800 members of Local 594 went on strike at the Pontiac plant and related truck development facilities on April 22 over demands for more jobs to replace retiring workers and ease a growing workload.
"The agrement meets our objectives on staffing levels and vacations. I think the membership will be pleased with it," Miller said.
"I feel bad that our members had to suffer for 85 days, but it was our turn in the barrel. Sometimes you have to suffer for the good of the many."
The strike was the longest local plant strike ever for GM and one of the industry's longest. UAW officials said the industry's longest walkout was a 101-day strike against Chrysler Corp. in 1950.

The strike is one of several the UAW has waged against GM this year. The automaker faces two new strike deadlines next week at a transmission plant in Warren, Mich., and a lighting plant in Anderson, Ind. A walkout at either plant could disrupt production at a number of plants.
